connections.why: Religious experience is offered as one argument among the philosophical questions about God's existence

Debate over describing religious experience raises questions about the meaningfulness of religious language
Scholars' arguments are what drive the later developments in religious belief
Responses to evil and suffering have reshaped how belief develops

The theories must be understood before they can be applied to concrete issues
The three theories sit alongside deontology and virtue ethics as the full theoretical toolkit
Medical ethics is the principal field in which the ethical theories are applied
Deontology and virtue ethics give competing verdicts on medical ethics dilemmas
Significant concepts in ethics lead into questions about the meaning of moral language
Beliefs are grounded in and justified by the religion's sources of authority
Beliefs and values are expressed through the practices that shape identity
Scholars interpret the sources of wisdom and authority within the tradition
Historical development frames how the religion engages with present-day society
Understanding sources of authority underpins study of the New Testament context
The historical and religious context shapes how texts about Jesus are interpreted
Philosophy of religion supplies the themes that the dialogue paper connects to the texts
Applied ethics provides the issues that textual study is brought into dialogue with
The religion's engagement with society feeds the dialogue between the texts and the modern world
Core Christian beliefs about Jesus inform the close reading of the New Testament texts
